name: Canada (Federal)

workplaceInjury.name: (Provincial boards handle workplace injury)
workplaceInjury.notes: Workplace injury compensation is administered provincially; federal layer relevant mainly to federally regulated employers via the provincial boards in most cases.

humanRights.name: Canadian Human Rights Commission
humanRights.notes: Applies to federally regulated sectors (banks, telecom, interprovincial transport).

accessibilityCompliance.name: Accessible Canada Act (ACA)
accessibilityCompliance.administeringBody: Accessibility Commissioner (Canadian Accessibility Standards Development Organization)

complaintProcess.name: Attempt to resolve with organization
complaintProcess.description: Contact the federal entity directly to resolve the accessibility barrier.

complaintProcess.name: File complaint with Accessibility Commissioner
complaintProcess.description: Submit formal complaint if unable to resolve directly. Commissioner may facilitate resolution or conduct investigation.
complaintProcess.typicalTimeframe: No statutory deadline for filing; investigation timelines vary

complaintProcess.name: Investigation and Resolution
complaintProcess.description: Commissioner investigates and may order compliance measures, publish findings, or impose administrative monetary penalties.
complaintProcess.typicalTimeframe: Varies - can take months to over a year depending on complexity

applicableTo: Federally regulated private sector (banks, telecoms, interprovincial transport, broadcasting)
priorityAreas: Procurement of goods, services, and facilities
Design and delivery of programs and services
accessibilityCompliance.notes: ACA came into force in 2019. Applies to federal jurisdiction entities. Does not replace provincial accessibility laws or human rights codes.

benefitPrograms.name: Canada Pension Plan Disability
benefitPrograms.description: Income replacement for contributors with severe and prolonged disability preventing any substantially gainful work.
evidenceTips: Longitudinal medical records showing onset and progression
Functional capacity details (what you can/cannot do)
Prognosis statements indicating severity and duration
Impact on ability to perform any substantially gainful work

appealPath.notes: Leave to appeal required; limited grounds

benefitPrograms.typicalProcessingTime: 120 days for initial decision (can be longer)

benefitPrograms.name: Employment Insurance Sickness Benefits
benefitPrograms.description: Short-term income support (up to 26 weeks) for insured workers temporarily unable to work due to illness, injury, or quarantine.
keyForms: EI Sickness Application (online via My Service Canada)
evidenceTips: Medical certificate stating inability to work
benefitPrograms.eligibility: Insured employment, 600 hours in last 52 weeks, medical certification

benefitPrograms.name: Canada Disability Benefit
benefitPrograms.description: New federal income supplement for working-age Canadians with disabilities (implementation in progress as of 2024-2025).
evidenceTips: Details pending regulations; expected to align with DTC eligibility
benefitPrograms.notes: The Canada Disability Benefit Act received Royal Assent in June 2023. Regulations being developed. Expected to provide income supplement for low-income persons with disabilities.

accommodationGuidance: Duty to accommodate to point of undue hardship (Meiorin test)
Interactive dialogue required between employee and employer
Consider modified duties, flexible hours, gradual return to work
Employer must explore all reasonable accommodations
Medical information limited to restrictions and accommodation needs
evidenceFocus: Accommodation history and what has/hasn't worked
limitationNotes: Human rights complaints: 12 months from last incident (federal sector - CHRC)
CPP-D SST appeal: 90 days from reconsideration
ACA complaints: No statutory deadline, but timely filing recommended
